# Heresay — the RUNTIME dependencies, pinned and hashed. (v1.48.0, audit G1/G2)
#
# ⛔ THIS FILE IS WHAT PRODUCTION INSTALLS, AND IT IS INSTALLED WITH
# `--require-hashes`. Both `make venv` and `deploy/deploy.sh` use it. Nothing
# resolves from PyPI at deploy time any more.
#
# Before this, every deploy ran `pip install argon2-cffi websockets cryptography`
# — unpinned, unhashed, re-resolving as root on the production host. A
# compromised release or a maintainer-account takeover landed in production on
# the next unrelated deploy, with nothing in the repo recording what changed, and
# the running versions were not reproducible from the checkout at all.
#
# ⚠ THREE DIRECT DEPENDENCIES, SIX LINES. The other three are the transitive
# closure (`argon2-cffi-bindings`, `cffi`, `pycparser`) and they are here because
# `--require-hashes` is all-or-nothing: a single missing transitive hash fails
# the install outright. That strictness is the feature.
#
# ⚠ `cryptography` is held at 50.x DELIBERATELY. 49.0.0 carried CVE-2026-69247
# (a Bleichenbacher oracle in `pkcs7_decrypt_*`), which this engine never called
# — it imports only `Fernet` — but "not currently reachable" is a statement about
# today's call graph, not a safety property. Do not pin back below 50.
#
# ⚠ `websockets` is held at the version the suite is proven against. 17.x exists
# and is not known-vulnerable; taking a major bump as a side effect of a security
# pin is exactly the unexamined change pinning is for. Upgrade it deliberately,
# on its own, with the suite as the evidence.
#
# TO REGENERATE (after editing requirements.in):
#     pip install pip-tools
#     pip-compile --generate-hashes --strip-extras --no-header \
#                 -o requirements.txt requirements.in
#
